newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on India skepticism.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on India skepticism.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on a setback from Tuesday's rally plus skepticism India will buy any wheat from the U.S., traders said.
There had been talk India soon may seek a large amount of wheat on the world market. That talk was magnified Tuesday by large purchases of wheat futures by key commercial Cargill Inc.
Traders said the market was overbought Tuesday which left it vulnerable for a profit-taking slip.
"It got a little overdone and they're taking some back today," a trader said.

Warmer weather in the U.S. winter wheat growing region which has diminished concerns about winterkill, also weighed on the market. But there was some talk early Wednesday about concern some Ohio wheat was harmed by the recent cold snap.
News Iraq was planning to buy wheat from France had little impact on futures because the U.S. was not expected to sell wheat to Iraq.
Wheat closed 1/2 to five cents per bushel lower, with March down three at $3.79-1/4 a bushel.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, below the 15,826 traded Tuesday, according to the CBOT.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 1,500 contracts, below the 2,956 traded Tuesday.
